extraction_scope: Worker-6 re-adjudicated mechanism claims from paper-local XML/PDF/supplement locators; automated framework placeholder claims were replaced with source-backed mechanism evidence and explicit limits.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Laminarin neutralization supports beta-1,3-glucan/cell-wall binding as an important step for KP-derivative candidacidal activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KP and KP-derivatives tested in Table 2
direct_assay_types: CFU inhibition neutralization assay with soluble beta-1,3-glucan laminarin
mechanism_claims.limitations: Neutralization supports cell-wall glucan involvement but does not alone define the downstream lethal pathway.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KP, H10S, and K10S induce intracellular ROS signals and reduce mitochondrial transmembrane-potential signal in C. albicans under the reported assay conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KP, H10S, and K10S in Candida albicans SC5314
mechanism_claims.limitations: Quantitative figure traces are not digitized; claim is limited to source-reported direction and assay context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-labeled KP/H10S/K10S interact with yeast cell wall and enter cells over time, with PI internalization and TEM-visible morphology changes reported for selected treatments.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: FITC-labeled KP, H10S, and K10S; TEM for H10S and K10S
mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy supports interaction/internalization/morphological damage, not a single fully resolved molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Annexin V/dead-cell assay supports apoptosis induction for most KP-derivatives, while K10S lacks a statistically significant apoptotic increase under the reported comparison.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KP and KP-derivatives in Candida albicans SC5314
mechanism_claims.limitations: Apoptosis evidence is derivative-specific and should not be generalized to K10S.
